finding: Persisted READY state contradicts the shipped driver: PASS exits the process before finally restores issuance; the MCP server does not enforce a one-send budget. Final live proof was not launched because the mandatory restore and single-gate laws cannot be guaranteed by this implementation.

findings.evidence: runE2E calls process.exit(0); the caller's finally containing restoreIssuance cannot execute. A standalone synthetic child-process counterexample exited 0 with BODY observed and RESTORE absent. No actual service was stopped for this check.

Each tools/call human_gate invokes humanGate again, registers a decision and calls transport.send. No one-shot reservation, already-in-flight rejection or consumed send budget is checked before sending. Asking the model to call exactly once is not an enforcement mechanism.

For verified option A the predicate accepts any transcript containing the letter a and continued_in_same_session=true. A synthetic transcript GATE_ANSWER=B CONTINUED_IN_SAME_SESSION=true passes the current predicate. It cannot independently prove option A consumption.

Deactivation searches only the current run's spool gate-store.json. The driver creates a fresh per-run spool, so prior runs' keyboards are not discovered by this path. No Telegram edit was attempted in this pre-send STOP.

process_observation.scope: Local CIM inventory of canonical issuance and project MCP gate/driver node processes; not a claim about remote Telegram consumers.

next: Repair the evidenced restore/send/consumption guards and cross-run stale-keyboard handling, then obtain a subsequent decision before another real gate. Integration closure is not eligible.
